claim_boundary: This proof counts one internally reproduced March 2020 Census M3 durable-goods boundary because two pre-decision first-report total new-orders monthly changes, two exact current official PDF hashes, exact 8:30 a.m. America/New_York report timing, a separately locked April 24 March event, immutable locks, separated truth labels, an explicit February persistence baseline, a no-probability persistence-or-one-known-increase program, deliberate TrialCourt failure, deterministic outputs, limitations, and a clean-worktree double rebuild all verify. Every selected PDF has post-release modification metadata, so current hashes are not represented as release-time byte identity. The March change is excluded from ReplayPack inputs and used only for a labelled post-event check that preserves its 1,560-basis-point lower-bound breach rather than widening the range. The April report's January and February snapshot values never overwrite the first-report inputs. M3 is not a probability sample, and the reported series is seasonally adjusted but not adjusted for price changes. The report's COVID-19 text concerns publication standards and does not establish causality or unaffected measurement. This proof does not establish forecast skill, calibrated coverage, statistical significance, price-adjusted output, manufacturing, inflation, pandemic, policy, sector, regional, or firm causality, external validation, deployment, investment performance, or user impact.

deliberate_failure_modes.description: TrialCourt must reject the retrospective one-initial-increase attempt rather than promote it as a validated forecast.
The immutable trial ledger retains one rejected decision.

absence_reasons.observed: The lock contains aggregate monthly changes reported in archived Census M3 releases, not firm, product, contract, transaction, price-adjusted, causal, or future-event observations. The March change is present only in the disjoint event lock.

naive_baselines.description: The decision-time baseline persists the February first-report total durable-goods new-orders change of 120 basis points.
The persistence-or-one-known-increase endpoints carry no probability, confidence, or coverage claim.
No confidence interval is represented as the FinReplay range; M3 is not a probability sample, so report-level sampling intervals are unavailable.
